newsitem.title: UK: Currency concerns drag Brady bonds lower.
newsitem.headline: Currency concerns drag Brady bonds lower.

text.p: Brady bond prices suffered sharp declines on Tuesday amid growing concerns about the spillover effect from recent turmoil in Eastern European and Asian currency markets, emerging market analysts said.

"The (Brady) market is getting nervous about currency concerns," said one trader at a U.S. investment bank in London. He said increased nervousness about exotic currencies triggered a spread widening of around 11 basis basis points on both Polish and Brazilian Brady bonds.
Traders attributed the declines in Poland and Brazil Brady bonds to general concerns about Brazil's growing current account deficit and slippage in the Polish zloty.
On a price basis, Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR fell 3/8 to 81-1/2 bid and Poland's par bonds PO275024=RR eased 5/8 to 58-3/4 bid.

Traders said Brazilian debt has come under pressure as mounting concern about Brazil's growing current account deficit has made investors extremely nervous that the Brazilian real could suffer speculative attacks.
But some analysts believe investors have used the Asian and Eastern European currency turmoil as an excuse to take profits following a spectacular rally in the emerging debt markets this year.

Although effective devaluations by the Czech Republic, Thailand and the Philippines over the past two months have heightened concerns for Brazil, some believe Brazil's reserve position is big enough to counter any potential attacks on its currency.

"It is inevitable there would be speculation (about Brazil) following events in Asia but I don't believe there will be any serious attack mounted let alone that any attack would be successful at the present stage," said Peter West, chief economist at BBV Latinvest.
"They have $57 billion reserves so people will think twice," he added.
West said Brazil's current account deficit is not in the danger zone as far as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) is concerned but it could be worrisome if it continued to keep growing.

Among other Latin credits, Mexican Brady prices were lower following news on Monday that a Mexican Finance Ministry official in charge of investigating money laundering was shot and killed in Mexico City.
"Mexico is wider on the back of the Mexican minister being shot," said one trader.
Mexican par bonds MX625L19=RR were 1/2 weaker at 79 bid and the country's discount bonds MXFLL19=RR were 1/4 lower at 93 bid.
